bugs.rootCause: The daemon had NO resolvable claude OAuth credential, so it dispatched claude with no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and claude died exit 65 (agent_error) in 5s before doing any work. Two facts combine, neither a hangar code bug. (1) The daemon env override HANGAR_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN was never set by the e2e harness. resolve() in crates/ainb-hangar-daemon/src/claude_cred.rs:130 checks that env var FIRST and only falls back to the keychain store when it is absent; the non-blocking path was simply not provisioned. (2) The keychain fallback is unusable in this session: the macOS login keychain is LOCKED for headless callers, so MacKeychainBackend.get presents a GUI unlock prompt nobody answers. Confirmed by the triager own repro: security find-generic-password hung the full 120s in a plain interactive shell, not just under the daemon. The daemon correctly raced that read against CRED_READ_TIMEOUT (run_loop.rs:77, 5s), logged 'keychain credential read timed out; dispatching without injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN', and fell through: exactly the fail-closed behavior PR #435 shipped this run. Re-touching claude_cred/run_loop would be the same-fix-different-layer trap; the real defect is that the verification never fed the daemon a credential and never gated on credential presence before dispatch.
bugs.fixPlan: Fix in the NEXT cycle driving (harness/preflight), no code PR. Provision the credential via the env-override path that bypasses the keychain (resolve() prefers HANGAR_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN and never touches the store when set). Steps: (1) Before 'ainb hangar daemon restart', obtain a claude OAuth token WITHOUT the locked keychain: first try reading ~/.claude/.credentials.json and extracting .claudeAiOauth.accessToken via jq; if absent, run 'claude setup-token' once in the interactive parent session to mint a long-lived sk-ant-oat token, and cache it under the job tmp dir for reuse across cycles (never print it). (2) Export that value as HANGAR_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN into the environment of the process that starts the daemon, so the daemon snapshots it into daemon_env; alternatively, as an env remediation, 'security unlock-keychain -p <pw> ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db' in the daemon session unblocks the store path, but the env override is cleaner and secret-safe. (3) Add a hard preflight gate in V0/V1: after daemon start and BEFORE any V3 dispatch, assert the credential source is 'env override'/'configured' (via the existing 'ainb hangar' cred status verb, backed by claude_cred::default::source) and fail-closed the whole cycle if it reports 'not set', so a missing credential surfaces at preflight instead of as a cryptic 5s exit-65 task failure. No hangar source change is warranted; the daemon behaved to spec.
